project.name: BackgroundRemover
project.what: Free, open-source background remover with the full six-stage cutout pipeline (not just a coarse mask), built on permissively licensed weights only. Replacement for remove.bg, whose API sunsets 2026-12-01 and moves to Leonardo.Ai.

workflow.branching: main is the default branch; branch before committing feature work
workflow.verified_means: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` green AND `.venv/bin/ruff check .` clean. Stage 2 additionally requires a real image through the CLI, since unit tests cannot cover it without weights.
workflow.spelling: British in prose and identifiers (licence, colour, normalised)

commands.torch_extra: uv pip install -e ".[torch]"  # ~2.5 GB, reference + ONNX export only

Stage 4 in the browser is a matrix-free conjugate-gradient solver over the matting Laplacian, restricted to the unknown band (~8% of pixels). VERIFIED against a pymatting fixture: mean |diff| 0.000161, max 0.0039. `npm run verify:matte`.
scripts/deform_compat.py: ONNX-compatible modulated deformable convolution built from grid_sample. Matches torchvision.ops.deform_conv2d to rel ~1e-15. Wired to `export_onnx.py --web`.

web/vercel.json with COOP same-origin + COEP credentialless. Verified crossOriginIsolated === true while still allowing an off-origin model fetch.
Model is now cached via the Cache API (bgremover-model-v1), not the HTTP cache, so a second visit is instant.
Fixed: ort.env.wasm.numThreads now checks crossOriginIsolated. Requesting threads without SharedArrayBuffer makes ORT fail to initialise rather than degrade.

SHIPPED AND WORKING END TO END. Model uploaded to https://huggingface.co/YheChen/bgremover-onnx (public, 210,363,856 bytes, byte-identical to local). VITE_MODEL_URL set on Vercel and redeployed; the HF URL is verified inlined in the shipped bundle.

Verified live on https://backgroundremover-theta.vercel.app with a 2.6 MP real photo (cat on snow, fur against low-contrast background) fetched cross-origin: WebGPU, clean cutout, fg=0.273, soft=0.029.
Fixed a self-inflicted bug: `await cache.put(url, res.clone())` drained the whole 210 MB before resolving, so the progress bar never moved. Body is now streamed and reported first, cached after.

EXPERIMENT 1 RESULT: switching stage 2 from BiRefNet_lite to DIS IS-Net (Apache-2.0) cuts the browser model forward from 22.41s to 0.86s on WebGPU -- a 26x speedup -- at equivalent quality (IoU 0.9908 between the two; fg 0.274 vs 0.273 on the test photo). Model is also smaller: 170 MB vs 210 MB.

The unlock was scripts/patch_maxpool_ceil.py. ORT-web refuses any graph with MaxPool ceil_mode=1. For 2x2/stride-2 pools over even-sized maps ceil and floor agree, so the attribute is decorative -- verified bit-identical (max|diff| = 0) before writing.

half_finished_that_will_break: models.py registers ben2 but it has never been exported or run, and BEN2 folds stages 3-4 into the model so it needs its own pipeline path, not just a different weights file. birefnet-hr is registered but unexported too.
Mixing torch (MPS) and onnxruntime in ONE process can abort at teardown with 'recursive_mutex lock failed'. Benchmark backends in separate processes.
REFINE's tile/band defaults are untuned guesses until the eval set exists.

web/public/models/ and web/public/ort/ are gitignored and must be regenerated on a fresh clone: `npm run copy:ort` runs automatically via predev/prebuild, but the model has to be exported by hand (see web/README.md).

gotchas: BiRefNet's HF checkpoint is fp16. Cast to fp32 for any CPU work (conv2d will not mix fp16 bias with fp32 input). Only go back to half on CUDA. This is the first thing that breaks if you touch _torch_model.

model(x) returns a LIST of length 1 holding a (1,1,1024,1024) tensor of raw LOGITS. Sigmoid is required and is not baked into the graph. export_onnx.py wraps this in FinestOnly so the ONNX graph is single-output.

torch>=2.9 routes torch.onnx.export through the dynamo exporter, which imports onnxscript. Without it the export fails with ModuleNotFoundError at the very END of a long trace -- easy to mistake for a model problem.

band_width in stage 3 is quoted against a REFERENCE_EDGE of 1024px and rescaled. A fixed pixel band is wrong in both directions: unscaled 12px on a 208x242 image put 41% of pixels in the unknown band, and stage 4 answered by softening every edge into a halo.

pymatting's default ichol preconditioner starts at shift=0, where the matting Laplacian is often not positive-definite enough; it recovers but prints PERFORMANCE WARNING and wastes a factorisation. matte.solve passes an explicit shift ladder starting at 1e-4.

LICENCE IS THE PROJECT'S DEFINING CONSTRAINT. BRIA RMBG-2.0/1.4 is CC BY-NC 4.0 and is the default model in rembg and several other wrappers. Adding it would make every downstream user non-compliant. models.py refuses it at construction; tests/test_registry.py asserts the refusal. Do not weaken this.
BiRefNet's repo licence is MIT but SOME variants were fine-tuned on private data and are non-commercial. Read the individual HF model card, not the repo licence, before registering a variant.
System python is 3.14.4; uv created the venv on 3.12.12. All deps (including torch 2.14 and onnxruntime 1.29) resolve on both, so requires-python is >=3.10 with no interpreter pin.
The first `uv pip install -e .` failed only because README.md did not exist yet — pyproject references it via `readme`. Order matters if the tree is ever rebuilt from scratch.

pymatting signatures verified against 1.1.15: estimate_alpha_cf(image, trimap) and estimate_foreground_ml(image, alpha, ..., return_background=False). Image must be float64 RGB in [0,1]; trimap float64 with 0=bg, 1=fg, anything else unknown.
Do not let EdgeMode.NAIVE become the default. It is stage 2 only and produces the hard halo-ed edges that make free tools look free.
Eval scoring is manual on purpose. IoU barely moves when a 3px hair fringe is wrong, which is exactly what users notice, so it is actively misleading here.
eval/out is flattened onto mid-grey deliberately: white backgrounds hide white fringing, black hides dark fringing.
Stage 3's band_width is the main quality/speed dial in the whole pipeline — only the unknown band goes to the expensive stage 4.
BiRefNet-HR is known to over-correct on some inputs. Newer is not automatically better; score it.

BiRefNet's HF checkpoint ships FP16 weights. CPU conv2d refuses to mix a half bias with a float32 input, so _torch_model casts to .float() and only returns to half on CUDA. This is the first thing that breaks if you touch that function.

BiRefNet returns a LIST of one tensor (1,1,1024,1024) carrying raw LOGITS, observed range about -28..19. Sigmoid is required and is NOT baked into the graph. segment.py applies it unconditionally for both backends -- do not make that conditional on value range.

ONNX export REQUIRES opset 22. BiRefNet's ASPP blocks use deformable convolutions and the ONNX standard schema only introduces DeformConv at 22. Below that, export succeeds but ORT rejects the graph at session creation: 'No Op registered for DeformConv with domain_version of 18'.

The CoreML execution provider FAILS on this graph: it claims 873 of 2869 nodes, fragments them into 228 partitions, then errors at execution with 'Unable to compute the prediction using a neural network model'. It is excluded from the defaults; override with BGREMOVER_PROVIDERS if you want to retest.
The ONNX export writes TWO files -- birefnet-general.onnx (10 MB) and birefnet-general.onnx.data (847 MB external data). They must travel together; ORT resolves the .data relative to the graph path.

band_width in stage 3 is quoted in px at a 1024px REFERENCE_EDGE and rescaled to the actual image. An unscaled 12px band put 41% of a 208x242 image in the unknown region and stage 4 answered by softening every edge into a halo. Pass absolute_band=True to opt out.
macOS has no `timeout` command. Do not wrap long commands in it.

There is NO MPS regression — an earlier reading of 116 s for a warm call was measured while a concurrent process was running the 847 MB ONNX export. Re-measured clean, MPS settles at ~2 s/pass (3.80, 6.77, 3.80, 2.43, 2.07) with allocation flat at 0.91 GB. MPS is the fastest path; ONNX/CPU (4.4 s cold, 6.3 s warm) remains the DEFAULT because it needs no torch install and is what the browser build consumes.

pymatting's ichol preconditioner shift list must start at 1e-3, not 1e-4. At 1e-4 the matting Laplacian is often still not positive-definite enough and every solve prints a PERFORMANCE WARNING — six of them per REFINE run. Verified that raising the shift changes the answer by at most 1/255: the preconditioner affects convergence rate, not the solution.
Benchmark timings in this repo are unreliable if anything heavy is running concurrently. Two separate wrong conclusions were drawn from contended measurements.

onnxruntime-web has NO DeformConv kernel on any provider. BiRefNet's ASPP uses deformable convs, so the browser graph must come from `export_onnx.py --web`, which swaps them for grid_sample. Native onnxruntime is fine with DeformConv at opset 22 -- this is a web-only constraint, but the web target is the product.

ort.env.wasm.wasmPaths must be built from document.baseURI. A bare './ort/' resolves against the bundled module's location (/node_modules/.vite/deps/ in dev) and 404s. onnxruntime-web must also be listed in vite's optimizeDeps.exclude, or the dep optimizer rewrites its internal runtime imports.

The ORT .wasm/.mjs runtime files are loaded by URL at runtime, so no bundler sees them. They are copied into web/public/ort by `npm run copy:ort`, wired to predev/prebuild. vite-plugin-static-copy was tried first and does not serve them in dev.
The torch.onnx dynamo exporter cannot convert torch.repeat_interleave with an implicit dim. Use Python scalars for anything known at trace time.

DO NOT ship an int8-quantised model to the browser. It is 159 MB vs 210, faster, and matches fp32 to IoU 0.9948 -- but only on native CPU. On onnxruntime-web's WebGPU path it returns a near-all-foreground mask: measured fg=0.974 against an expected 0.443, and 14.5s instead of 1.9s. Caught only by running it in a real browser. fp32 ships.

fp16 conversion via onnxconverter_common yields a malformed graph ('Type Error: Type (tensor(float16)) of output arg') when GridSample is block-listed. It would halve the 210 MB download, so it is worth another attempt, but it is not a one-liner.

COEP must be 'credentialless', not 'require-corp'. require-corp blocks the cross-origin model fetch; dropping COEP entirely loses SharedArrayBuffer and so single-threads the WASM fallback. credentialless is the only value that satisfies both. Dev and prod headers are kept identical so this cannot regress silently.
Vercel Hobby: 100 MB max per uploaded file and 100 GB/month bandwidth. The 210 MB model cannot go there, and even a 100 MB one would cap the site near a thousand cold visitors a month.

MODEL HOSTING, options evaluated 2026-09-08. GitHub Releases is RULED OUT: release-assets.githubusercontent.com sends NO access-control-allow-origin header at all, even when the request carries an Origin, so a browser fetch() is blocked by CORS. Verified against a known-public asset. Do not retry it. jsDelivr is also out (20 MB per-file cap vs a 210 MB model).

Vercel Blob is viable in principle but needs a store provisioned in the dashboard first: `vercel blob list` errors with 'VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN and BLOB_STORE_ID must both be set'. CLI auth alone is not enough.

Hugging Face remains the recommended host: free, CDN-backed, no bandwidth cap on public repos, and it does send CORS headers. Needs `hf auth login` with a WRITE-scoped token -- a Read token authenticates fine and then fails at upload.

Zero-account fallback if HF is ever unavailable: split the model into sub-100MB parts and serve same-origin from Vercel, sidestepping CORS entirely. Costs Vercel bandwidth -- 210 MB per cold visitor against Hobby's 100 GB/month is ~475 visitors, and exceeding the cap PAUSES deployments.

Never `await cache.put(url, res.clone())` before reading a large response body: put() drains the full stream before it resolves, so any progress reporting downstream is dead on arrival. Stream and report first, cache the assembled bytes after. This only reproduced against the real remote URL -- a same-origin local model was fast enough to hide it.
Live perf datapoint: 2.6 MP photo = 62s on WebGPU on the deployed site, main thread blocked throughout. The 1.9s figure from local testing was a 208x242 image and is not representative.

onnxruntime-web REFUSES MaxPool with ceil_mode=1 ('using ceil() in shape computation is not yet supported'). For 2x2/stride-2 pools over even feature maps the attribute is decorative; scripts/patch_maxpool_ceil.py strips it and REFUSES to write if the output changes. This is what unblocked IS-Net on WebGPU.

IS-Net needs DIS normalisation (mean 0.5, std 1.0) and output[0], with sigmoid ALREADY baked in. Feeding it ImageNet normalisation scores IoU 0.16 against a known-good reference instead of 0.99 -- a plausible-looking wrong mask, not an error. Per-model contracts now live in MODELS in web/src/stages/segment.ts.

Running inference on the WASM EP appears to poison the JS stages that follow: with BiRefNet/WebGPU stages 3-6 took ~7.9s in-browser, with ISNet/WASM the same stages took ~37.8s, while node measures 4.6-4.7s for both. Unexplained; suspect worker-thread or heap contention. Another reason to move the pipeline into a Web Worker.
